Fixed. The three CommonMark examples from the report (518, 519, 532) now match the spec, and the full spec and unit suites pass. **Cause:** `link()` and `reflink()` in `src/Tokenizer.ts` accepted an outer `[...](...)` even when its link text already contained a link. The inner link was produced, and the outer one wrapped it, giving nested `` elements. **Fix (`src/Tokenizer.ts`):** - `outputLink` now returns `undefined` for a link (not an image) whose tokenized text contains a link at any depth. A new helper, `hasNestedLink`, does the recursive check. Images are still allowed to contain links, as CommonMark requires. - `reflink` falls back to a literal `[` text token in that case, the same as its existing "no definition found" path. - The outer brackets are then literal text and the inner link wins, which is the behaviour the report expects. **Verified:** - `[foo [bar](/uri)](/uri)` → `

[foo bar](/uri)

` - `[foo [bar](/uri)][ref]` → `

[foo bar]ref

` - `[foo *[bar](/uri)*](/uri)` and `![foo [bar](/url)](/url2)` still behave correctly. - `node --test test/run-spec-tests.js`: 1781/1781 pass. - `node --test test/unit/marked.test.js`: 44/44 pass. **Test data change:** examples 518, 519 and 532 were marked `shouldFail: true` in `test/specs/commonmark/commonmark.0.31.2.json` and `test/specs/gfm/commonmark.0.31.2.json`. The runner treats a passing "should fail" example as an error, so I removed those markers. Nothing else in the spec files changed. I did not add new tests, since the existing spec examples cover this behaviour.
